summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a complex medical history including diastolic heart failure, type II diabetes, chronic kidney disease, alcoholic cirrhosis, and Crohn’s disease was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and generalized edema over one week. She had gained 40 pounds and required three pillows to sleep. Evaluation revealed bibasilar crackles and significant lower extremity edema. Although BNP was not elevated, she was treated for acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation with intravenous Lasix and an increase in oral torsemide to 60 mg daily. Her renal function was acutely impaired with a creatinine of 2.2, likely due to cardiorenal syndrome, but she maintained good urine output. She showed clinical improvement in respiratory status and was discharged home with plans to follow up with cardiology, nephrology, and primary care. All other comorbidities, including diabetes, liver disease, and chronic pain, remained stable during admission.
